rationale: Existing non-security duplication across expanded src/scripts/workers scope. Exact fragment/file-pair hashes block new findings; no security finding is excused. 2026-11-11: retired database tools removed; their clones left the baseline. Two existing clones in check-supabase-performance-advisor.ts (its usage text and option parsing) were reported against the deleted check-supabase-security-advisor.ts and are now reported against run-supabase-cli.ts: same code, new pair. 2026-11-12: two unreferenced R2 scripts removed with their shared clone; the check now fails when recorded debt is gone but still budgeted, so the budget only goes down. 2026-11-12: the retired-backend removal deleted source-backend code whose clones were recorded; their fingerprints left the baseline and the budget was lowered. Ignore entries that matched no clone were dropped from .jscpd.json. 2026-11-13: part 5 of the retired-backend removal deletes code without touching any clone, so the same 9 clones are a slightly larger share (0.09% to 0.10%). 2026-11-13: the touch-screen video card's full-card play target was removed (one tap opens the post), so its clone of the desktop card's play target left the baseline. 2026-11-17: the lead-count hook reads through one shared request, so its two copies of the same fetch left the baseline. 2026-11-20: the header's phone menu (signed-in and signed-out lists) is the same recorded clone; its 'Register' and '+ Post' buttons changed style (button hierarchy, ledger group 66), which changed the fragment's text, so its fingerprint was replaced and the budget lowered (190 to 186 lines). 2026-11-28: the posting forms batch stopped using one recorded clone (it left the baseline) and the budget was lowered (8 to 7 clones, 186 to 136 lines); the event schemas share one block of new event fields instead of repeating it.
